news.summary: EU leaders put forward Pablo Hernández de Cos to head the ECB. In London, Imperial Brands responded to Altria’s interest after European shares had closed higher. US exchanges were closed for Thanksgiving.
news.coverage: Through 09:58 SGT. Imperial’s response was released at 01:18 SGT and the European Council notice at 06:50 SGT. The index figures are European closes dated 26 November. NYSE had no Thursday cash session.
happened: The European Council proposed Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde, who is due to leave on 7 February 2027. Leaders also proposed Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB’s executive board.

Imperial’s board said it had received no approach and had held no talks about Altria’s possible bid. Altria had already disclosed that it was considering a cash offer and discussing a possible disposal of part of the business with a third party.
The STOXX Europe 600 closed at 636.98 versus 626.03, and the FTSE 100 at 10,609.30 versus 10,426.90. Each rose 1.75% in Thursday’s European session, which ended after Singapore midnight.
key_points: The European Council still has to consult the European Parliament and the ECB Governing Council before a formal appointment. The presidency carries an eight-year term.
Altria has yet to announce a firm bid or a price. Imperial’s response adds the target board’s account of contacts.
watch: Watch for the two consultations and the European Council’s formal decision.
Altria faces a 17:00 London deadline on 24 December to declare its intentions, unless the UK Takeover Panel grants an extension.

bonds.summary: Kiwibank set the initial coupon on its NZ$200m Tier 2 issue at 5.17%. Bids at the final margin exceeded NZ$340m. The first optional redemption date comes five years before maturity.
bonds.coverage: The books closed at 06:57 SGT, the coupon was announced at 07:24 and final terms followed at 07:40. The US corporate index levels are dated 24 November. A newer observation was unavailable in the verified FRED releases.
happened: Kiwibank allocated the full NZ$200m at a margin of 120 basis points over the swap rate. The issuer reported about 1.7 times coverage at that margin, excluding lead managers’ trading interest.
Interest is fixed at 5.17% per year until 4 June 2032. If the notes remain outstanding, the coupon resets quarterly to the three-month bank bill rate plus 120 basis points.
The final terms set maturity for 4 June 2037. Kiwibank expects issuance on 4 December 2026 and NZX quotation under KWB3T2 on 7 December.
key_points: The 5.17% figure is the initial contractual coupon. Secondary-market yields will depend on traded prices.
A holder could remain invested beyond June 2032 because redemption at the first call date is optional.
watch: Check settlement on 4 December and the first eligible traded price after quotation.
Compare subsequent US corporate spread readings with the last verified observations of 98 bp for investment grade and 372 bp for high yield.

earnings.summary: Two New Zealand half-year results show why profit and revenue need to be read alongside asset sales. Green Cross Health’s medical disposal drove most of its reported profit. Burger Fuel’s store transfer reduced the sales it consolidated.
earnings.coverage: Both issuers reported unaudited six-month results to 30 September in NZ dollars. NZX released Green Cross at 03:30 SGT and Burger Fuel at 08:52 SGT. These are separate company results from New Zealand.
happened: Green Cross Health reported NZ$196.7m in profit attributable to shareholders, including a NZ$188.1m gain on its medical division sale, completed on 31 July.

In its continuing pharmacy business, revenue rose 9% to NZ$197.7m and operating profit rose 3% to NZ$7.0m. The company cited pressure on margins from a shift toward high-value, lower-margin medicines.
Burger Fuel reported NZ$948,749 in profit after tax, up 11.7%. Operating revenue excluding IFRS 16 interest income fell 3.9% to NZ$11.8m after the Ponsonby store passed to a franchisee.
key_points: Green Cross’s pharmacy operating profit offers a baseline for assessing the continuing business after the disposal.
Burger Fuel said operating revenue would have grown excluding the ownership change. It ended September debt-free with NZ$5.26m cash.
watch: Track pharmacy operating profit alongside sales in Green Cross’s first full half following the sale.
Compare Burger Fuel’s next half-year revenue with a period that also excludes company-operated Ponsonby sales.

economy.summary: Chinese industrial profits grew 20.1% year on year in October. In Tokyo, inflation accelerated on the measure excluding fresh food, while the measure stripping out both fresh food and energy slowed.
economy.coverage: Tokyo figures are the preliminary mid-November 2025-base series released on 27 November. China released January–October results at 09:30 Beijing and Singapore time, 28 minutes before cutoff.
happened: China’s statistics bureau reported RMB6.737tn of profits for industrial enterprises above its reporting threshold in January–October, up 16.0% year on year on a comparable basis. October alone rose 20.1%.
Over the ten months, Chinese manufacturing profits rose 17.5% and mining profits rose 38.8%. Profit in electricity, heat, gas and water supply fell 14.8%.

Preliminary Tokyo ward CPI rose 2.8% year on year in November after 2.7% in October. Excluding fresh food, inflation rose to 2.9% from 2.6%. Excluding both fresh food and energy, it eased to 2.5% from 2.6%.
key_points: The Chinese profit data cover industrial enterprises above the designated size. Across this group, the ten-month operating revenue profit margin rose 0.45 percentage points to 5.69%.
The two Tokyo measures moved in opposite directions. The figures cover Tokyo’s wards and offer an early indication ahead of the national November release.
watch: Check the national Japanese CPI release for whether the divergence seen in Tokyo also appears across Japan.
Track Chinese manufacturers’ margins and receivables as well as headline profits. Receivables at end-October were 10.5% above a year earlier.

news.summary: Singapore will challenge the proposed US tariff during the consultation. Taiwan shares recovered part of Wednesday’s fall, while the latest US close showed weaker tech shares and a modest gain for the Dow. Altria also disclosed interest in a possible cash bid for Imperial Brands.
news.coverage: Full Thursday Singapore window, reconstructed from the 15:05 edition and dated releases. Altria’s 12:56 London disclosure falls here. The completed US stock prices are from Wednesday’s New York close. The NYSE observed Thanksgiving on Thursday.
happened: Singapore’s trade ministry said it would ask USTR to reconsider a proposed tariff of up to 20%, net of existing Section 301 duties and subject to exemptions. The ministry cited a US bilateral trade surplus of US$33bn in 2025.

An Eldridge-led consortium announced an agreement to acquire Lukoil International. The group said the upstream portfolio produces about 350,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day. The deal requires US sanctions approval, due diligence and other closing conditions.
Taiwan’s TAIEX closed at 39,151.81, up 956.38 points from 38,195.43. Thursday’s gain recovered roughly half of Wednesday’s 1,926.92-point loss.
At the Wednesday New York close, Nvidia fell 3.91% to US$149.30. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% to 23,585.80 and the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78. The Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95.

At 20:56 SGT, Altria disclosed that it was considering an offer for Imperial Brands, likely solely in cash. It also confirmed talks with a third party about buying part of Imperial. Altria had not committed to a bid.
key_points: The US proposal leaves room for a 10% rate if the US and Singapore reach qualifying terms. The consultation matters for both the rate and the goods covered.
Current output from Lukoil’s portfolio measures the size of the assets. The announcement establishes a conditional agreement, with ownership transfer still pending.
Altria’s disclosure began the UK takeover timetable. The disclosure gave neither a bid price nor a binding commitment.
watch: Look for Singapore’s formal submission and any revisions to the US product exemptions or rate.
Watch for the US Treasury’s sanctions decision on the Lukoil deal and the consortium’s closing notice.
Look for a firm Altria offer or a statement withdrawing its interest by the 24 December deadline, subject to any permitted extension.

bonds.summary: S&P placed Nvidia on negative watch over governance concerns. In the Treasury market, seven-year notes sold at 4.708% and benchmark yields fell across the two- to thirty-year maturities. The UK completed its bank capital review and outlined a consultation on domestic lending.
bonds.coverage: The auction and par curve are dated 25 November in the US and became available on 26 November in Singapore. The Nvidia action was checked against Reuters reporting. The latest verified ICE figures were for 24 November, before the rating news. UK policy figures are estimates from the 26 November Financial Stability Report.
happened: Reuters reported that S&P put Nvidia’s AA credit rating on CreditWatch Negative after the CEO’s departure and return raised questions about board oversight. The review was open at cutoff.
The US Treasury offered US$44bn of seven-year notes. The high yield was 4.708%, the coupon 4.625%, and bids totaled 2.43 times the amount awarded. The notes mature on 30 November 2033.
On the 25 November US par curve, the two-year yield fell 2 bp to 4.61%, the five-year fell 4 bp to 4.65%, the ten-year fell 6 bp to 4.85%, and the thirty-year fell 6 bp to 5.24%.

The Bank of England said its capital review would lower normal-times Tier 1 requirements for major UK banks by the equivalent of around 50 bp of risk-weighted assets in aggregate. The Prudential Regulation Authority plans to consult on lower minima connected to domestic lending.
key_points: A negative watch raises the possibility of a downgrade. Nvidia still carried an AA rating in the report.
The ten-year yield fell more than the two-year yield. The difference narrowed from 28 bp to 24 bp over the US session.
The 50 bp estimate combines review measures and varies by bank. The FPC’s benchmark for aggregate system-wide capital requirements is around 13%.
watch: Follow S&P’s resolution of the watch and any Nvidia board changes it cites.
Compare the next ICE US high-yield and investment-grade observations with their 24 November levels of 372 bp and 98 bp.
Watch the PRA consultation for how the UK capital changes would apply to lenders with different domestic exposures.

earnings.summary: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare raised full-year guidance after a strong half in hospital care. Insurer Tower reported lower annual profit as large-event costs rose from the previous year.
earnings.coverage: Both NZX releases appeared at 08:30 NZDT, or 03:30 SGT, on 26 November. Both periods ended 30 September. Fisher & Paykel Healthcare reported six months and Tower reported twelve. Currency is NZD.
happened: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare reported first-half operating revenue of NZ$1.25bn, up 15%, and net profit of NZ$291.4m, up 37%. Hospital revenue rose 22% to NZ$841.5m, while homecare revenue grew 4%.
The company raised fiscal 2027 net profit guidance from NZ$525m–565m to NZ$565m–605m. Its interim dividend increased from 19 to 26 New Zealand cents per share.
Tower reported full-year profit of NZ$52m versus NZ$83.7m a year earlier. Gross written premiums rose 3% to NZ$620m. Five large events cost NZ$23.9m, compared with NZ$7.2m in the prior year.
key_points: A NZ$23m US tariff refund helped lift Fisher & Paykel Healthcare’s gross margin to 66.4%. The company put margin excluding that refund at 64.6%.
Tower’s 10-cent final dividend comprises 6 ordinary cents and 4 special cents. Including the interim payout, the year’s dividends total 15 cents per share.
watch: Compare Fisher & Paykel Healthcare’s second-half hospital sales and margin with its upgraded full-year guidance.
Track Tower’s large-event costs against its NZ$50m fiscal 2027 allowance when assessing the NZ$60m–70m underlying profit guidance.

economy.summary: Korea tightened policy as it raised growth forecasts and expected inflation to stay above target. The Fed’s regional contacts reported US growth in eight districts alongside little improvement in consumer spending. Singapore factory output increased 6.1% year on year in October.
economy.coverage: Korean figures use the 26 November policy decision. The Fed released the Beige Book at 14:00 EST on 25 November, or 03:00 SGT Thursday. District reports are qualitative. EDB released its October estimate at 13:00 SGT on Thursday.
happened: The Bank of Korea voted 5–2 to raise its base rate by 25 bp to 3.25%. The two dissenting members preferred 3.00%.

The bank projects GDP growth of 3.9% in 2026 and 4.1% in 2027, up from 3.3% and 2.9% in August. It cited exports and semiconductor investment. Its 2027 headline inflation forecast rose from 2.3% to 2.4%.

The Fed’s November Beige Book reported slight to moderate growth in eight districts and little change in four. Contacts described flat overall consumer spending, softer housing activity and modest manufacturing growth.

Singapore’s EDB reported October factory output up 6.1% year on year, or 12.1% excluding biomedical manufacturing. Seasonally adjusted output rose 7.1% from September. Precision engineering rose 54.1% year on year as semiconductor equipment production increased, and electronics output rose 6.6%.
key_points: The Korean forecasts assume that strength in semiconductors supports the domestic economy. How far that income reaches households remains an uncertainty in the bank’s outlook.
The Beige Book draws on contacts through 16 November. Its regional descriptions cover a later period than Wednesday’s US third-quarter GDP estimate and use a different method.
Singapore’s 7.1% monthly change uses seasonally adjusted output. Its 6.1% annual growth compares October with October a year earlier.
watch: Track Korean core inflation against the bank’s 2.6% forecast for 2027 and watch for stronger household consumption.
Compare upcoming US spending and housing releases with the uneven conditions regional Fed contacts described.
